newsitem.title: MEXICO: Analysts pleased with Desc '96 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Analysts pleased with Desc '96 earnings.

text.p: Earnings results from Mexican conglomerate Desc Sociedad de Fomento Industrial (Desc) showed the company weathered Mexico's weak domestic economy last year by focusing on exports, analysts said on Friday.
Desc on Thursday posted 1996 net earnings per share of 6.62 pesos per share, compared with an average prediction of 6.10 pesos from four analysts previously surveyed by Reuters.

"That's a positive earnings surprise," said Bond Snodgrass, an equity analyst at Mexico City's Abaco brokerage, who stressed the EPS figure was derived using the average rather than year-end number of shares outstanding for 1996.
"It was slightly better than we expected across the board," said Daniel Goldstein, of ING Barings. "We were a little conservative in our estimates, but we do prefer to err on the side of caution."

Desc's earnings were driven by its auto parts division, whose net sales were up 22.1 percent from 1995 to 4.406 billion pesos, while the operating margin was up to 16.7 percent from 11.6 percent due to cost controls.
The auto parts division accounted for 37 percent of Desc's consolidated sales for the fourth quarter in 1996.

Net sales for the chemicals division were down 8.8 percent from 1995, meanwhile, but analysts noted that the operating margin was up to 18.2 percent, compared with 16.8 percent in 1995. "I'm surprised chemicals did as well as they did," Goldstein said.
Desc's chemicals' division, which relies more on the domestic market for sales, accounted for 41 percent of the group's net sales in the fourth quarter of 1996.
For Roberto Galvan, equity analyst at the Bursametrica consultancy, Desc's strength lay in its diversity.
"1996 was a good year for manufacturing exporters in general in Mexico, just as 1995 was good for commodities exporters," Galvan said.
"The peso stabilized in 1996 and commodities prices fell, so companies exporting products with value-added were favored, like Desc's autoparts division," he added.

Analysts were optimistic about Desc's future, saying the company should be able to play either the domestic economy or continue its export drive. But a stronger peso in real terms could cut into autoparts exports.
A recovery in the domestic market and government infrastructure projects could favor Desc's other divisions, however, particularly agribusiness, consumer products and real estate, he added.
